prompt:
Scene:
A square photograph at early morning with a 35mm full-frame camera, positioned on a fjord cliff. Wet Nordic atmosphere, low cloud ceiling hanging just above the 1000-meter cliff tops, diffuse overcast light tinted cold grey-green.

Subject:
A fjord where a traditional waterfall used to fall from the cliff edge is now completely inverted: the river above the cliff turns and rises as a 200-meter column straight into the low clouds. At the base, water arrives from the fjord surface and climbs the cliff face, leaving wet streaks on the dark granite. A lone fishing trawler sits directly beneath, its deck workers visibly staring upward.

Important details:
Cold oceanic palette: slate green water, black-grey granite, white mist. Wet cliff surfaces have believable water paths showing the reverse flow. The trawler has realistic proportion against a 1000-meter cliff — a toy on the water. Seabirds circle the base of the rising column. Atmospheric moisture softens distant cliffs into pale silhouettes.

Use case:
Lift-studies single 1/5 — reverse-gravity event in a Nordic fjord.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no cruise ships with branding, no oil platforms, no cartoon, no fantasy creatures.
